title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (10-20Y nominal, 1:40pm ET)
source: TSY: three treasury.gov/treasurydirect.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-10, all naming this operation. (1) The REVISED Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding quarter), home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Buyback-Schedule.pdf (HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes), masthead For Publication September 9, 2026 and PDF metadata naming BuybackCalendar-August-2026-Updated_20260909.docx distilled 2026-09-09 09:44:39 ET — its 9/10 row reads announce 9/9, operate 9/10 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/11, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 10Y to 20Y, min $0, max $6 BILLION. This supersedes the August 5 schedule the entry previously cited, which sat unrevised for 21 days after press release sb0607 and still read max $2 billion. (2) The operation announcement itself, treasurydirect.gov BBPA_20260910174000.xml (HTTP 200), announcementDTM 2026-09-09T11:00:00-04:00, maxParAmountRedeemed 6000000000, operationStartDTM 2026-09-10T13:40:00-04:00, 40 issues eligible, maturity range 2037-02-15 to 2046-08-15. (3) The results, BBR_20260910174000.xml and fiscaldata buybacks_operations for operation_date 2026-09-10 — the operation ran and settled its terms, so the date is now a matter of record rather than a scheduling claim. Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> TSY: on the standing instruction in this event own ledger kill switch 5, checked 2026-09-10
notes: Lands 40 minutes after the 30Y reopening closes on the SAME day (auction 1:00pm ET, buyback 1:40pm ET) and is the first long-end liquidity-support operation on or after sb0607's 09-09 effective date — so its cap should step from the scheduled $2B to the announced $4B/operation minimum, though Treasury has not yet published the updated schedule. Note the sector is 10-20Y, NOT the 20-30Y bucket the reopened bond sits in; the next 20-30Y operation is treasury-buyback-20y30y-2026-09-24. The schedule's own maturity range for this operation, read off the PDF text layer 2026-09-02, is 09/11/2036 - 09/10/2046, so the bond being auctioned that morning (CUSIP 912810UW6, maturing 2056) is NOT eligible for it — the same-day support is adjacent-sector in the literal sense, not a bid for this CUSIP. UPDATED 2026-09-03 by this event's own pulse check, on a direct fetch of the schedule PDF: sb0607's promised updated buyback schedule is STILL UNPUBLISHED 15 days on — the posted schedule's masthead reads 'For Publication August 5, 2026' and the 09-10 row still says max $2 billion, so the 09-09 operation announcement remains the only path to a hard number. Two scale facts from the same document argue the step-up is normalization, not stimulus: the 1Mo-2Y, 3-5Y, 5-7Y and 7-10Y liquidity operations ALREADY carry $4B caps (only the two long-end buckets sat at $2B), and a $12.5B cash-management buyback runs 09-09, one day prior and ~3x the entire long-end increase. And the $4B is a floor, not a point estimate: Bessent told CNBC on 2026-08-20 that buybacks 'could be more than the 4 billion per issue', conditioned on market conditions. Discovered during the treasury-30y-bond-2026-09-10 pulse-check adjacency sweep. UPDATED 2026-09-08 by this event's own pulse check: the schedule PDF re-fetched direct is still 125,547 bytes with masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026' and max $2 billion on the 09-10 row — 20 days after sb0607 and still no revised schedule — and none of the nine Treasury press releases newer than sb0607 (sb0613 through sb0621) touches buybacks, so the 09-09 operation announcement remains the only path to a hard number. Material correction from the full fiscaldata buybacks_operations series (all 53 of 2026's operations, fetched direct 2026-09-08): the 11-of-11 full-cap fills this bucket recorded in 2026 is an artifact of its $2 billion cap, NOT evidence Treasury wants to buy more. Every nominal-coupon bucket that already carries a $4 billion cap fills it only partially — 7Y-10Y 7 percent of cap, 5Y-7Y 25 percent, 2Y-3Y 45 percent, 3Y-5Y 50 percent, for $1.28 billion mean accepted, 32 percent of cap and 0 of 12 full fills. The discriminator across all 46 nominal-coupon operations of 2026 is cover (total par offered divided by announced maximum), behaving as a threshold: at cover of 6x or more, 23 of 24 operations filled the cap; below 3x, only 6 of 19 did. At a $4 billion cap this bucket's own 2026 range of 3.7-18.0x cover becomes 1.85-9.0x, with 9 of 11 operations below the 6x line. So a partial fill on 09-10 would be Treasury's price discipline rather than weak demand, and it is a live outcome rather than an exotic one. UPDATED 2026-09-10 by this event own D-0 pulse check, from three direct primaries — the operation RAN and every open parameter resolved. THE ANNOUNCED MAXIMUM PRINTED $6 BILLION, 50 percent above sb0607 $4 billion floor and above every branch this entry had priced; Bessent 2026-08-20 CNBC remark that buybacks could be more than the 4 billion per issue was literal. RESULT: $10.489 billion offered, $5.187 billion accepted, 1.75x cover, 86 percent fill, 23 of 40 eligible issues. That is the SECOND-LOWEST offer volume and the LOWEST cover of this bucket twelve 2026 operations (2026 mean $20.17 billion; next-lowest cover 3.70x on 8/11), and its FIRST non-full fill — the regime shift the 2026-09-08 note predicted. Four CUSIPs took $4.284 billion of the $5.187 billion (83 percent), all deep-discount low-coupon 2040-2042 paper: 912810ST6 $1,703 million, 912810TF5 $1,294 million, 912810SW9 $706 million, 912810TK4 $581 million; every zero-accepted issue was an older higher-coupon pre-2016 30Y bond. THE STRUCTURAL CHANGE MATTERS MORE THAN THE SIZE: the revised schedule published 2026-09-09 states a number ONLY for this operation. Every subsequent long-end row — 9/24, 10/1, 10/8, 10/15, 10/27 and 11/4 — reads = or > $4 billion, while the 7Y-10Y, 2Y-3Y and 1Mo-2Y buckets keep hard $4 billion figures and TIPS keep $500 million and $750 million. Treasury replaced the published long-end CEILING with a published FLOOR and moved the actual maximum to a per-operation disclosure one business day ahead, so a cover ratio for any future long-end operation is uninterpretable unless the announced maximum is recorded alongside it. No press release accompanied any of this: Treasury press index fetched direct 2026-09-10 shows sb0622 through sb0626 newer than sb0621, covering Iran sanctions, health-care fraud and a cyber-scam action, and none touching buybacks.
